newsitem.title: CYPRUS: New measures designed to help Cyprus bourse mooted.
newsitem.headline: New measures designed to help Cyprus bourse mooted.

text.p: Incentives to help the fledging Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) are being considered and could be announced next month, Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou said on Thursday.
"There are five suggestions under study and it is a matter of one or two weeks for them to be announced," Christodoulou told a news conference. "They will be substantial measures," he added.
The 41-share bourse started operating in an official capacity on March 29, 1996, replacing years of unofficial trading held under the auspices of the Cyprus Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
Some suggestions under consideration include easing the listing requirements for a company to be listed on the exchange and introducing taxation allowances on dividends and income.

Last month the government announced plans to change the current income tax regime, so that owners of shares of listed companies can enjoy tax and dividend tax incentives for the purchasing of initial public offerings.
It also announced a 15 million cash injection to various quarters of the economy.
Christodoulou said the bourse responded positively to the incentives. "The government will announce additional measures if the economy needs it," he said.
